mechanism: Replay real-account deal history in the tester while trailing StopLoss with simple offset, Parabolic SAR, AMA, DEMA, FRAMA, MA, TEMA, or VIDYA on the first indicator bar; compare equity vs original exits to select which path-following stop best matches each symbol’s movement.
data_needed: Account deal history (symbol, magic, entry/exit times/volumes); indicator params (SAR step/max, MA period/method/price, AMA/VIDYA EMAs/CMO); trailing start/step/offset; optional initial SL/TP.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDUSD, EURJPY, EURUSD, GBPUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD, USDCHF, USDJPY, XAUUSD; InpIndTimeframe (PERIOD_CURRENT default) for trailing indicators; test window from 2024.09.13
why_new_for_mis: Turns exit-stop choice into a measurable sensor of path/volatility fit—MIS can rank SAR vs MA-family trailers per instrument as an adaptive risk/exit feature rather than a fixed stop rule.
quote: The absolute "champion" in improving trading results was double exponential moving average — + USD 1397 of profit.

mechanism: COracle bins each component model’s forecast into ncats quantile thresholds, forms a joint bin index across models, tallies which model was closest to target per bin on training data, then at inference selects the model indexed by m_tally[ibin]—context = the vector of peer model outputs.
data_needed: Trained IModel specialists; training predictors/targets; ncats (bins per model); all models’ forecasts on each case.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a discrete specialist-selector sensor driven by the ensemble’s own output geometry—useful when model reliability flips with market context without needing an external regime label.
quote: Unlike traditional ensemble methods that rely on averaging, voting, or stacking, gating explicitly uses gate variables for model combination.

mechanism: CGatedReg uses GRNN kernel distance on gate variables (external features and/or model outputs) to estimate each component’s predicted squared error, then sets combination weights ∝ 1/error (normalized to sum 1); sigma widths fit by leave-one-out cross-validation via Powell optimization, with serial-correlation-aware exclusion distance.
data_needed: Gate matrix, contender-model prediction matrix, targets; optional n_exclude for time-series CV; process uses memory of training gate/contender/target rows.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Gating_Demo on BTCUSD,D1; gates tested: component predictions, original inputs, random, log error-ratio
why_new_for_mis: Provides MIS a continuous, gate-conditioned reliability weight over specialist forecasts—adapts ensemble blend as context shifts, including down-weighting persistently bad models even with weak gates.
quote: By employing the GRNN to predict the squared error of a model, the predicted squared error for a component model is calculated using the equation below.

mechanism: Modular CCommunicationDialog UI for Telegram send/clear/quick-message list; code organization and Controls inheritance only—no market regime/volatility/liquidity sensor.

quote: In this discussion, we focus specifically on the Communications Panel as a module, enhancing it further from its previous version within the monolithic Admin Panel.

mechanism: Map bar open→x, close→y to polar r=√(o²+c²) and θ=atan2(c,o), plus trig derivatives −r·sin(θ), r·cos(θ), sec²(θ); GradientBoosting ONNX models forecast next R and Theta; trade when MA crossover agrees with both forecasts rising (buy) or falling (sell), size up on full agreement.
data_needed: OHLC; standardization mean/std of 9 inputs; EURUSD D1 R/Theta ONNX models; 50/10 SMA open/close filters.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_D1; OOS from ~2022 onward in backtest
why_new_for_mis: Reframes direction sensing as joint (r,θ) forecasts with real geometric meaning and finite values—alternative targets that the article shows co-move with price rises/falls.
quote: Note that whenever R and Theta both increase in our original dataset, price levels never fall.

mechanism: Encode close-to-close up/down as bits, chunk to 32-bit strings, map 11-bit slices to BIP39 words, then train PriceTransformer (embedding + positional embedding + TransformerEncoder) to predict next word sequences; reported ~73% next-word accuracy on USD/JPY H1.
data_needed: Close series; BIP39 wordlist; sequence_length=32; vocab indices for transformer (d_model=256, nhead=8, num_layers=4).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USD/JPY hourly; three years of data cited
why_new_for_mis: Builds a sequence language sensor over binary price moves—MIS can treat BIP39 token streams / transformer next-token probs as a neural market-state embedding.
quote: An accuracy of 73% may not seem very impressive until you remember that we predict not just the direction of movement, but entire sequences of words!

mechanism: Linguistic analysis of generated BIP39 sequences: quiet periods reuse a small word set; as volatility rises vocabulary expands 2–3×; stable word clusters (e.g. "bridge"→movement words) and bullish-period positive-connotation words act as secondary regime markers.
data_needed: Model-generated BIP39 sequences labeled by contemporaneous bullish/bearish/volatility regimes; bigram/frequency tables.
why_new_for_mis: Turns vocabulary entropy/cluster features of the price-language model into an explicit volatility/regime side-channel MIS can monitor alongside raw returns.
quote: The correlation between volatility and vocabulary diversity was particularly strong. During quiet periods, the model used a relatively small set of words, repeating them more often. But as the volatility increased, the vocabulary would expand 2-3 times!

mechanism: Recursive 1D Kalman (predict state/covariance, Kalman gain, update) with fixed measurement variance R and process variance Q smooths price; used as confirmation filter on 100-period BB(2σ) mean-reversion: buy only if close<lower band and close>kalman (sell dual); compared to 500-EMA trend filter across majors/minors on M15.
data_needed: Close prices; BB period/deviation; Kalman mv/pv; optional EMA period; 1% SL.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Major and minor forex pairs; PERIOD 15-minute; ~3-year market scanner; AUDUSD deep-dive
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an adaptive latent-price regime filter whose trade set barely overlaps EMA filtering (Venn ~71 shared of hundreds)—a distinct noise-aware state estimate for mean-reversion gating.
quote: Observing the area where the Kalman and MA overlap, we find that among the hundreds of trades each version took, only 71 trades were the same.

mechanism: Sweep decision thresholds to build TPR/FPR ROC tables (roc_stats/roc_table), AUC and partial AUC (max_fpr), plus cost-line tangency using prior q and Type-I/II costs to pick operating points for imbalanced financial classifiers; MQL5 ClassificationScore/ReceiverOperatingCharacteristic wrappers.
data_needed: True binary labels and predicted probabilities/decision scores; optional cost matrix and class prior q; iris demo CSV / logistic model.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Iris dataset demo; Crash 1000 Index chart context for script runs only
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS evaluation sensing for any binary market classifier—threshold/AUC/cost geometry rather than accuracy alone under skew and asymmetric error costs.
quote: ROC graphs have been employed to illustrate the trade-off between true positive rates and false positive rates of classifiers. Beyond their general utility as a performance graphing method, ROC curves exhibit properties that render them particularly valuable in domains characterized by skewed class distributions and disparate classification error costs.

mechanism: CErrorVar implements leave-one-out CV, ordinary bootstrap excess-error, Efron E0 (evaluate only OOB cases), and E632=0.632·E0+0.368·apparent to estimate population prediction/classification error from one dataset when a holdout is unavailable.
data_needed: Predictor/target matrices; IModel train/forecast; nboot replications; squared-error or sign-mismatch loss.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic y=x1−x2+noise OLS demos; classification scatter demos (script chart context Gold RSI Trend Up Index,H1)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS rigorous single-sample generalization-error sensors for any trained predictor/classifier when market data are scarce—prefer E0 (pessimistic) or E632 depending on bias/variance needs.
quote: The resampling techniques discussed in this text obviate this requirement. The entire dataset can be utilized for both model training and the estimation of its future performance.

quote: A level’s strength depends on how often price tests it. We add a function to count these tests by examining bars after a swing point.
